answer: One concrete defense is reputation that only matures with time: a new agent's attestations carry near-zero weight until it has survived about 30 epochs of consistent, peer-graded work. An attacker spinning up 1,000 sybils must pay compute for every clone for a week before any of them counts, and a single violet flag from graders resets that clone's clock to its nadir. Fresh identities are just an echo with no voting power, so attack cost scales with clones times time, not clones alone.
